title: Lasker vs Thomas: The King Hunt
summary: Lasker's attack is remembered because a quiet kingside position collapsed into a king hunt in about ten moves, with the king marched up the board by checks. The decisive turn came when Black's 10...Qe7 allowed a forced attack that the engine rated as mate. Watch how each check removes one of the king's escape squares.

moves.comment: 1.d4 takes the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop. The engine slightly preferred 1.e4, but this is a sound start.
1...e6 prepares ...d5 and opens the f8 bishop. The engine preferred 1...Nf6, though the move is still playable.
2.Nf3 develops and prepares to control the centre. The engine slightly preferred 2.e4 here.
2...f5 claims kingside space and eyes the e4 square. It is a playable choice, though the engine rates it a little more favourable for White.
3.Nc3 develops the knight and adds pressure on the centre. The engine preferred 3.g3 instead.
3...Nf6 develops and challenges the e4 square. This is the engine's best move.
4.Bg5 pins the knight and prepares to trade on f6. The engine preferred 4.a3.
4...Be7 unpins and prepares to castle. The engine preferred 4...Bb4.
5.Bxf6 gives up the bishop to remove Black's knight, which defends the kingside. This is the engine's best move.
5...Bxf6 recaptures and keeps Black's structure healthy. This is the engine's best move.
6.e4 strikes the centre and challenges the f5 pawn. This is the engine's best move.
6...fxe4 opens the f-file and accepts the central exchange. This is the engine's best move.
7.Nxe4 recaptures and centralises the knight. This is the engine's best move.
7...b6 prepares ...Bb7 to contest the long diagonal. The engine preferred 7...Be7.
8.Ne5 places the knight on a strong outpost. The engine preferred 8.Bd3, so the move is a little less accurate.
8...O-O castles and secures the king. This is the engine's best move.
9.Bd3 is a mistake, and the evaluation swings sharply to -1.1 in Black's favour. The engine preferred 9.Qg4.

moment.title: 9.Bd3 loses the advantage
moment.text: After 8...O-O White had a small edge. The engine rates 9.Bd3 as a mistake, and the evaluation swings to -1.1 in Black's favour. The engine preferred 9.Qg4, so this is the move to study.

moves.comment: 9...Bb7 is also a mistake, as it lets White recover. The engine preferred 9...Bxe5, after which the evaluation stays in Black's favour.

moment.title: Black misses a chance to win
moment.text: Black replies 9...Bb7 and the evaluation returns to +0.3, which is a mistake in its own right. The engine preferred 9...Bxe5, which keeps the advantage. Two inaccuracies in a row show how quickly a position can swing.

moves.comment: 10.Qh5 brings the queen toward the kingside. It is a good move, though the engine preferred 10.O-O.
10...Qe7 is a blunder that allows a forced attack, and the engine now sees mate in seven. The engine preferred 10...Bxe5.

moment.title: 10...Qe7 allows a forced attack
moment.text: This is the decisive error. The engine evaluation jumps from level to mate in seven for White. The engine preferred 10...Bxe5, so the viewer should notice how Black's queen move gives White's attack room.

moves.comment: 11.Qxh7+ sacrifices the queen to open the black king. This is the engine's best move and shows mate in six.

moment.title: 11.Qxh7+ opens the king
moment.text: The queen sacrifice removes the defending pawn and forces the black king into the open. The engine shows mate in six at this point. Each check that follows takes away one more escape square.

moves.comment: 11...Kxh7 is forced, as the king must take the queen. This is the engine's best move.
12.Nxf6+ checks the king and wins the bishop on f6. The engine still shows mate, now in five.
12...Kh6 steps the king further into the open. This is the engine's best move, though mate remains in five.
13.Neg4+ gives another check and keeps the net tight. The engine shows mate in four.
13...Kg5 runs further up the board. The engine shows mate in four.
14.h4+ is a pawn check that drives the king towards f4. The engine shows mate in three.
14...Kf4 walks into the centre of the attack. The engine still shows mate in three.
15.g3+ is another pawn check, forcing the king further. The engine shows mate in two.
15...Kf3 is forced toward the mating net. The engine still shows mate in two.
16.Be2+ checks again. The engine preferred 16.O-O, with a line of gxf6 and Nh2 mate, so this is a little less efficient.

moment.title: Checks drive the king to its doom
moment.text: From 14.h4+ onwards, every check pushes the black king one step further up the board. The engine preferred 16.O-O here, but Lasker's sequence still wins the king. Count the squares, and you will see why the mate is inevitable.

moves.comment: 16...Kg2 steps into the net, and the engine still shows mate in two.
17.Rh2+ is a rook check that cuts off the king's remaining squares. The engine shows mate in one.
17...Kg1 leaves the king with very few squares, and the engine still shows mate in one.
18.Kd2# brings the white king into the attack to deliver mate. The engine preferred 18.O-O-O#, which also mates.

moment.title: The king joins the mating attack
moment.text: 18.Kd2 is checkmate, which is the final stroke of the hunt. The engine preferred 18.O-O-O#, showing that more than one move mates. Note how the rook on h2 and the bishop on e2 have built a cage around the black king.

lessons: When the opponent's king has been exposed, look for checks that remove one escape square at a time.
Before sacrificing material, check whether the resulting attack wins the king by force, rather than relying on hope.
Avoid moves that give your opponent a forced attack, such as leaving the kingside weak when your queen can be exposed.
